title: Machine-learning models estimate perioperative transfusion risk in lumbar fusion
summary: Using retrospective records from 1,905 patients undergoing posterior lumbar interbody fusion at one hospital, the study compared five models after XGBoost feature selection. XGBoost had the highest validation-set AUC (0.958), with accuracy 0.903 and recall 0.897. This random split within a single-center cohort is internal validation; external performance and improved surgical decisions or patient outcomes are not established.
ai_technology: XGBoost, logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and other machine-learning classifiers

evidence.tested: Five models were compared on a held-out validation subset of retrospective records from 1,905 lumbar-fusion patients at one hospital.
evidence.unknown: External validation and effects on care decisions or patient outcomes were not reported.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost selected features and the trained models estimated perioperative transfusion risk from clinical records.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
